subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should the memory-search watcher failure be mitigated by a default periodic sync fallback for existing users, or should the default remain opt-in while watcher recovery is improved separately?
rationale: The code bug is clear, but the proposed default changes background memory sync behavior for existing installations and is compatibility-sensitive under the repository policy.

options.title: Adopt the default fallback
options.body: Refresh and land the linked PR or equivalent with a 30-minute default, explicit `0` opt-out, docs/schema alignment, and proof that interval sync rescans stale memory.

options.title: Keep fallback opt-in
options.body: Leave the default at `0` and solve only watcher recovery/diagnostics, accepting that users must configure `intervalMinutes` for a periodic safety net.

options.title: Narrow to watcher health
options.body: Require a watcher heartbeat/restart design instead of changing interval defaults, which avoids background work but leaves a larger owner-design task.

recommendation.title: Adopt the default fallback
recommendation.body: Refresh and land the linked PR or equivalent with a 30-minute default, explicit `0` opt-out, docs/schema alignment, and proof that interval sync rescans stale memory.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged memory-core watcher rework that now owns the closest current-main behavior around memory watcher coverage and fallback paths.
